Problem: In triangle PQR, angle Q is not 90 degree, PQ is 8 cm, and QR is 12 cm. X is a variable point on line PQ. Line XY is drawn parallel to QR, intersecting PR at Y. A line is drawn from Y parallel to PQ, intersecting QR at Z. QR is bisected at point B and PB forms an angle α (alpha) with PQ. Find the least possible length of line segment XZ given that α = 60 degrees.

<reflection>
The given data are $PQ=8$ cm, $QR=12$ cm, $\angle Q \neq 90^\circ$, $X$ is a variable point on $PQ$, $XY \parallel QR$ with $Y$ on $PR$, and a line through $Y$ parallel to $PQ$ meets $QR$ at $Z$. $B$ is the midpoint of $QR$, and $\angle PBQ=\alpha=60^\circ$. The target is the least possible length of $XZ$.
The triangle similar to $\triangle PXY$ is $\triangle PQR$ (because $XY \parallel QR$, with $X$ on $PQ$ and $Y$ on $PR$), not $\triangle QXR$.
Correct the similarity statement to $\triangle PXY \sim \triangle PQR$ and then use the given data, including the midpoint condition and $\alpha=60^\circ$, to determine the geometry.
